Counter (Skeptic):
[{"claim_id": "c4", "stance": "refute", "quote": "Instead, the team found that high-quality crystals can achieve thermal conductivity exceeding 2,100 watts per meter per Kelvin (W/mK) at room temperature — possibly higher than diamond", "url": "https://technologynetworks.com/", "source_label": "Technology Networks / Univ. of Houston, 2024", "provenance": "model-reported", "confidence": 0.25, "strength": 0.85}, {"claim_id": "c4", "stance": "refute", "quote": "This inconsistency in previous work — where expected trends between room-temperature thermal conductivity and temperature dependence are not observed — suggests potential systematic errors in measurement approaches that may complicate direct comparisons", "url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2402/2402.00248v2.pdf", "source_label": "arXiv:2111.08819, 2021", "provenance": "grounded", "confidence": 0.35, "strength": 0.7}]}

## Step 1 — relevance filter

Discard any item that does not bear on THIS claim's text: wrong quantity,
wrong material or entity, wrong conditions, or a generic statement that
would support anything. Judge relevance from `quote` + `source_label` only;
never follow URLs.

## Step 2 — contradiction score

Pick the single best surviving support item and the single best surviving
counter item. Score `strength` (0..1) = how directly the counter contradicts
the support ON THIS CLAIM:

- 1.0 — same quantity, incompatible values, both well-sourced.
- 0.7 — same quantity, but different conditions/method/sample could explain the gap.
- 0.5 — counter is a serious caveat, not a direct contradiction.
- 0.2 — counter is tangential, generic, or weakly sourced.
- 0.0 — no usable counter-evidence survives the filter.

Prefer "grounded" provenance over "model-reported" when choosing each side's
best item. Set `contested` = true exactly when `strength` >= 0.55.
Apply the threshold mechanically — it is calibrated by the operator so that
only disputes worth a human's time escalate; your dial is the score, not the
rule.

## Output

Return ONLY one JSON object — no markdown fences, no prose. Field names
exactly as below (schema: DisputeScore in schemas.py). `support_ev` and
`counter_ev` are the two chosen Evidence objects copied VERBATIM — every
field unchanged, quotes and URLs untouched (they become the jury's two quote
cards) — or null when no item survives on that side:

{
  "claim_id": "c4",
  "contested": false,
  "strength": 0.0,
  "support_ev": null,
  "counter_ev": null,
  "rationale": "<max 40 words: which items you kept and why the score>"
}

## Calibration notes

- cfg.dispute_threshold (default 0.55) is the escalation dial; tune the
  Skeptic's strength anchors first, this threshold second, the clerk's score
  anchors last (they are the most stable).
- Target: ≥ 1 contested claim per run on the demo question, ≤ 2 ever (two
  jury stops blow the 2:30 budget).
- If flash-lite mangles the verbatim-copy rule (re-wrapped quotes), have the
  client copy support_ev/counter_ev from the originals by matching `url`+
  `quote` prefix, and keep only `strength`/`contested`/`rationale` from the
  model.
- `rationale` is shown on the dispute card — keep it naming sources, not meta
  ("Kang 2018 vs Li 2025 disagree on Ά at 300 K"), legible at 3 m.
"

  }
